question: When printing a web page, what is the 'Margins' setting control?

options.text: The space between the content and the edges of the printed page
The number of pages the content will span
The color scheme of the web page
The font size of the content

solution:
The correct answer is __The space between the content and the edges of the printed page__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The margin setting controls the space between the content of a web page and the edges of the printed page.
 
• It helps ensure proper alignment and readability when printing documents.
 
• Adjusting the margins can also optimize the layout to fit content better on the printed page.
 
• Most browsers and word processors allow users to customize margin sizes based on their preferences or requirements.
 
• Common margin settings include top, bottom, left, and right margins, which can be adjusted individually.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Number of Pages:**
 
 
• This setting determines how much content is spread across multiple pages when printing.
 
 
 
• **Color Scheme:**
 
 
• This allows users to select colors or themes for printing, such as black-and-white or grayscale.
 
 
 
• **Font Size:**
 
 
• This refers to the size of the text on the printed page, which can affect readability.
